_about: Taste packs for motion design. Each one is distilled from a reference that works (credited in `from`). bin/motion-brief.py picks one from the brief and writes the full prompt in the <inputs>/<direction>/<structure>/<build>/<gotchas>/<start> grammar. Add a pack when a new reference earns it; never copy a creator's film, take the rules.

shared.easing: critically damped spring 1-(1+w t)e^(-w t), w 12-40, nothing passes its target; exponential ease-in/out for wipes, presses and exits
shared.beat: every move starts 0.05 s before its beat so it lands on it; something happens on every beat; no hold longer than half a second
shared.frame_rules: 1080x1920 at 30 fps (render 4 motion-blur sub-frames); text inside the Instagram safe box x 59-918, y 278-1536; nothing at rest within 90 px of the safe edges
shared.honesty: every number, name and claim on screen comes from the user's words, their brand files, channel-facts.json or a cited source; ask or leave it off
shared.muted: the story must read with the sound off

packs.name: Drafting inks (one line, three inks)
packs.from: heyiamnick's Claude motion-designer showreel prompt (awesome-opus5-5-videos, heyiamnick-119558)
packs.fits: introduce a person, a tool or a system; explain how something is built; a loop for a profile; technical, crafted, nerdy
packs.concept: one pencil line gets promoted twice (graphite on paper, wire on a blueprint, light on black) and never leaves the screen
inks: PAPER: cream, 60 px blue grid at 13% (every 5th at 26%), pencil lines wobbling on slow sines re-phased 8x a second, doubled, diagonal hatching fills, hatched type with a doubled outline
BLUEPRINT: flat blue, white grid, clean 3-4 px white lines, hidden edges dashed, fine clean hatching
HOLOGRAM: black, cyan grid, cyan lines with a 30% white core, fills are 8 px scan lines whose thickness follows the light; no glow
packs.camera: locked and front-on like a drafting table; objects turn, the camera never moves
transitions: paper to blueprint: a shape that floods the frame with a hard edge
blueprint to hologram and back to paper: one horizontal scan line
arc: DRAFT: the hero word is pressed flat into the line
TYPE: words live in a slot between two rails that resize to fit each word
CURVE: pen-tool handles bend the line; copies fan; travelling sines
MORPH: the line curls into a circle (length kept), then triangle, square, hexagon; hatching builds
TILE: honeycomb; hatching floods solid; the centre cell floods the frame into blueprint
SOLID: each hexagon becomes a cube seen corner-on; they merge; perspective turns on
GEAR: the front face grows teeth; a meshing gear train steps on eighth notes
PANEL: the cube unfolds into six panels that become a dashboard of the user's real numbers
DATA: a playhead runs at the real time; a cursor clicks a mode switch; a scan line turns it to light
LIGHT: the chart stands up as lit solids
WAVE: their tops join into a travelling surface that flattens into the line
END: the line lifts into the rail and the hero word rises back; the last frame is the first
packs.engine: motion/engine/mg.js (inks, pencil stroke, hatching, curl, polygon morph, cube, gear, flood and scan wipes)

packs.name: One shape, many UI states
packs.fits: an app, a SaaS product, a feature list, an onboarding flow; clean and Dribbble-level
packs.concept: one element is never cut: it morphs size, radius and colour through 8-12 UI states (button, loader, toggle, tabs, chart, player, command palette, toast)
packs.camera: a slow drift on the background only
transitions: state to state: the same element morphing; never a cut, never a fade
furniture: one serif-italic word per state, swapped on the morph
arc: press
load
expand to a card
list
chart
toggle
toast
back to the press (loop)
packs.engine: HyperFrames + GSAP transforms (formats/motion-design.md) or mg.js polygons

packs.name: Loud launch poster
packs.fits: a launch, a waitlist, a drop, a product with real clips and photos; energetic and graphic
packs.concept: a poster world that never stops moving: an op-art sunburst, a 3D box, a ticket, real media playing inside the design

type.family: Archivo 900 condensed for names, expanded for headlines; Geist Mono for labels

packs.camera: never stops: a slow 1.03-1.07 push on every scene
transitions: a disc floods the frame into the drop
everything folds back into the opening disc
furniture: a ticker that runs round the frame edge at the end
stickers with a white die-cut border and soft shadow
arc: open: sunburst + wordmark typing
drop: a 3D box with the big claim
story: a ticket that types its rows
proof: real clips in discs or phones with counters
CTA: a ticket that tears
loop: fold back to the disc
packs.engine: mg.js + HyperFrames video clips for the real media

packs.name: Editorial cream explainer
packs.from: Skillry CreatorMotion's house style (skillry.dev/ai-videos/ai-motion-graphics): pick the effect by what changes on screen
packs.fits: a talking-head explainer, a YouTube or Reels point, a claim with a number, a before/after, a step list, a chapter
packs.concept: the visual is chosen by the change in the sentence: a number grows (sequential bars, accumulation blocks), two options compared (paired result swap), a step added (synchronized checklist), a new chapter (character reveal), a definition (reframe)

type.family: a condensed italic display face for headlines, a clean grotesque for labels

packs.camera: still; the layout does the moving
transitions: the presenter swaps sides with the chart
furniture: a fine grid on cream paper
arc: hook line in big italic
the change, drawn (bars / swap / checklist / reframe)
the proof or the number
the takeaway line
packs.engine: mg.js (bars, cards, wipes) composited over the talking head with bin/composite-layers.py

packs.name: Words as architecture
packs.from: gdgtify's 'BUILD THE FLOOR' spoken-word prompt (awesome-opus5-5-videos, gdgtify-929495)
packs.fits: a quote, a manifesto, a short speech, a founder line; literary and monumental
packs.concept: each key word has a structural role (a lintel, a load, a support, an opening, a platform) and the last line stands on what the earlier words built

type.family: a high-contrast serif for the speech, a heavy grotesque for load-bearing words, a restrained mono for timing marks

packs.camera: still; pressure comes from the layout
transitions: the next composition is revealed through an aperture made by a letter's counter
arc: the line under pressure
the load lowers on fine rules
a support word lifts it
a second support levels it
the final line stands on the floor the words built
